summary: fix(e-boekhouden): tighten cache directory/file permissions and re-chmod on rewrite and on every readCache call that reaches an existing file, fresh or expired
reason: This CLI was printed at generator v4.22.0, before the cache-permission hardening in cli-printing-press (commit ae1f46baf, 2026-07-20) landed upstream. writeCache used 0o755/0o644 (world-readable), exposing cached invoice/relation/ledger/mutation responses to other local users on a shared machine. Separately, os.WriteFile's perm argument only applies when creating a file, so even after tightening the mode, an existing cache file written under the old 0o644 code stayed world-readable across an upgrade until manually deleted. A third gap surfaced by a later Greptile pass on PR #1867: a legacy 0o644 file still inside the 5-minute cache TTL was returned by readCache's cache-hit path directly, never reaching writeCache's chmod, so it stayed world-readable for up to 5 minutes after an upgrade. A fourth gap surfaced by a still-later Greptile pass caught the fix for the third gap being incomplete: the chmod ran only after the TTL check, so an *expired* legacy file returned a cache miss before ever being chmod'd -- if that key's next live fetch never succeeded (a failed request, an API outage), the file stayed world-readable indefinitely, not just for the 5-minute TTL window. A fifth gap, from the next Greptile pass: the chmod's error return was discarded, so if the permission correction itself silently failed (e.g. a filesystem that doesn't support changing permissions), readCache still served the cached financial response from a file it never confirmed was no longer world-readable. The chmod now runs on every readCache call that reaches an os.Stat'd file, before the TTL check, regardless of hit or miss, and a failed chmod is now treated as a cache miss rather than ignored.
call_sites: if err := os.Chmod(cacheFile, 0o600); err != nil { return nil, false }  // readCache, right after os.Stat succeeds and before the TTL check
validated_outcome: go build ./... and go test ./... pass. TestWriteCache_RechmodsExistingFile, TestReadCache_RechmodsFreshLegacyFile, and TestReadCache_RechmodsExpiredLegacyFile all confirmed to fail without their respective fix and pass with it. The chmod-error-refuses-cache-hit branch (fifth gap) has no dedicated test: triggering a real os.Chmod failure on a file this process owns needs root or filesystem-specific behavior (no-permission-bits filesystem, immutable flag) not reproducible portably in a plain temp-dir unit test -- verified by code reading and the existing suite passing, not a targeted regression test. Greptile review threads on PR #1867 resolved for the initial permission finding, the existing-file re-chmod-on-write finding, the fresh-file re-chmod-on-read finding, the expired-file re-chmod-on-read finding, and the discarded-chmod-error finding.
